## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Avaṭaphaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 468) is a canonical verse text preserved within the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Like many biographical poems in this collection, it records the devotional deeds and past karmic fruit of an elder (thera). SuttaCentral records five translations across five modern languages, though it provides no dedicated English title [SuttaCentral]. No further discussion of this specific text appears in the supplied secondary literature.
According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the text exhibits substantial Pali-internal text reuse, with 82 matching passages identified across 33 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. The largest reuse partner is the commentary on the Theragāthā (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo), which contains 13 matching segments (most notably §1.1–3.2 aligning with §4267–4271) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, nearly the entire text (§0.1–8.1) is duplicated in another apadāna of the same name, *Avaṭaphaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 506) [DharmaNexus]. Extensive formulaic parallels and shared verse segments are also found throughout other fruit-offering poems in the Therāpadāna, such as *Tālaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 511), *Ajeliphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 509), *Avaṭaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 383), and *Amodaphaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 510) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus detects no cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora meeting the threshold score [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
